title: The 14-Day Rotation

background.schedule: 2 meals on most days; restaurant breakfast on weekends; Wednesdays are protein-shake days

tuna.title: Spicy tuna–avocado rice bowl
steps: Microwave rice and drain tuna.
Mix soy, lime and sriracha; toss with tuna.
Add avocado and cucumber over rice; drizzle sauce.
tuna.tip: Toss in chili crisp for crunch; measure it if using more than a teaspoon.

gingerbeef.title: Sticky ginger beef noodles
steps: Cook noodles according to package.
Brown beef in a skillet; add broccoli and cook until hot.
Stir together soy, honey, sesame oil, garlic and ginger; add to pan, toss with noodles.
gingerbeef.tip: A splash of rice vinegar or lime gives the sauce more bite.

lemonpotato.title: Lemony chicken and potato bowl
ingredients: 225 g cooked chicken breast or thigh
Lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper
steps: Microwave halved potatoes until tender, about 7–9 minutes.
Warm cooked chicken if preferred.
Whisk olive oil, Dijon, lemon and oregano; toss everything together.
lemonpotato.tip: Use cooked chicken strips or rotisserie chicken to keep this nearly no-prep.

fajitas.title: Smoky chicken fajita rice bowls
steps: Season chicken with paprika, cumin, salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in oil until cooked to 74°C/165°F. Add peppers and onions; cook until tender-crisp.
Serve half over rice with salsa and lime. Refrigerate the other half promptly for Thursday lunch.
fajitas.tip: Double the vegetables if hungry; the second portion makes Thursday lunch easy.

fajitaleft.title: Fajita black-bean bowl
ingredients: 1 portion cooked fajita chicken and peppers from Tuesday
¾ cup drained canned black beans
steps: Microwave rice, leftover chicken and beans until piping hot.
Add corn, salsa and lime.
fajitaleft.tip: Leftover cooked chicken should be refrigerated promptly and used within 3–4 days.

salmon.title: Maple–Dijon salmon with potatoes
steps: Heat oven or air fryer to 200°C/400°F. Toss potatoes with oil and seasoning; start cooking them first.
Combine Dijon and maple syrup; brush salmon and cook until done (about 10–14 minutes depending on thickness).
Steam beans; finish with lemon.
salmon.tip: For less cleanup, use foil or a parchment-lined tray.

meatballs.title: Garlicky meatball marinara pasta
ingredients: 220 g cooked lean turkey or beef meatballs
steps: Cook pasta and heat meatballs to package directions.
Warm oil and garlic; stir in marinara and spinach until wilted.
Toss with pasta and meatballs; finish with chili flakes and basil.
meatballs.tip: Look for meatballs without cheese if you dislike that flavour.

chili.title: Smoky turkey and black-bean chili
ingredients: Chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and salt
steps: In a pot, sauté onion and pepper in oil; brown the turkey thoroughly.
Add tomatoes, beans and spices. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Eat one portion; cool and freeze at least one additional portion for next Monday.
chili.tip: Makes about 3 portions; top with chopped onion, cilantro and hot sauce.

porkchop.title: Garlic–lime pork chops and sweet potato
ingredients: 350 g sweet potato, cut in wedges
steps: Air-fry or roast seasoned sweet potato wedges at 200°C/400°F until crisp, about 18–25 minutes.
Season pork with paprika and garlic; pan-sear to safe doneness and rest.
Toss cabbage with vinegar and lime; plate together.
porkchop.tip: A little hot sauce in the slaw makes it brighter.

thaicurry.title: Thai red shrimp curry
steps: Heat curry paste in a skillet for 30 seconds.
Add coconut milk and vegetables; simmer until vegetables are hot.
Add shrimp and cook until opaque; serve over rice with lime.
thaicurry.tip: Curry pastes vary dramatically in heat—start with 1 tbsp.

chilipotato.title: Chili-loaded baked potato
ingredients: 1 frozen portion of homemade turkey chili
steps: Pierce potato and microwave until tender, turning once.
Reheat thawed chili until piping hot.
Split potato, spoon chili over it and add onion and hot sauce.
chilipotato.tip: If the portion is small, add a handful of extra beans.

oregano.title: Lemon–oregano chicken rice bowl
ingredients: 225 g raw chicken breast or thigh
Garlic, dried oregano, salt and pepper
steps: Season chicken with garlic, oregano, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Pan-sear in olive oil until chicken reaches 74°C/165°F.
Serve with warm rice and tomato-cucumber salad dressed with lemon.
oregano.tip: A generous amount of lemon keeps this tasting fresh without a cream sauce.

peanutnoodle.title: Thai peanut chicken noodles
ingredients: Lime juice, chili sauce and warm water
steps: Cook noodles and chicken; chicken should reach 74°C/165°F.
Whisk peanut butter, soy, lime, chili and enough warm water for a pourable sauce.
Toss noodles with chicken, crunchy vegetables and sauce.
peanutnoodle.tip: Add extra lime and chili instead of extra peanut butter for a stronger flavour.

tacoskillet.title: Smoky taco beef skillet
ingredients: Salsa, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika
steps: Brown beef in a large skillet; add pepper and taco spices.
Add beans and corn; cook until heated through.
Serve over warm rice with diced avocado and salsa.
tacoskillet.tip: For a little heat, add chipotle in adobo or pickled jalapeños.

shrimpmango.title: Chili–lime shrimp mango bowl
steps: Sear thawed shrimp in oil until opaque and cooked through.
Mix diced mango and cucumber with lime and chili flakes.
Serve over rice and finish with cilantro.
shrimpmango.tip: Frozen mango chunks can work too—thaw before serving.

harissa.title: Harissa chicken and chickpea tray bake
ingredients: 225 g chicken breast or thigh, diced
steps: Heat oven or air fryer to 205°C/400°F.
Toss chicken, chickpeas and vegetables with harissa and oil. Roast, turning once, until chicken is cooked to 74°C/165°F.
Squeeze lemon over everything.
harissa.tip: Harissa is spicy and aromatic; start with less if unfamiliar.

tunabeans.title: Tuna, white bean and potato salad
ingredients: Lemon juice, parsley, garlic and pepper
steps: Microwave potatoes until tender; cool slightly.
Whisk oil, lemon and garlic.
Toss with tuna, beans, tomatoes and parsley.
tunabeans.tip: Capers or a teaspoon of Dijon make the dressing sharper.

koreanbeef.title: Korean-style sticky beef bowl
steps: Sear beef strips over high heat and remove when cooked.
Cook broccoli and mushrooms until tender-crisp.
Return beef; toss with soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger. Serve over rice.
koreanbeef.tip: Optional sesame seeds and scallions add texture.

tomatocurry.title: Tomato–coconut chicken curry
ingredients: 250 g chicken breast or thigh, cubed
Curry powder, garam masala, garlic and ginger
steps: Sear seasoned chicken until browned.
Add tomato, coconut milk, garlic, ginger and spices; simmer until chicken reaches 74°C/165°F.
Stir in spinach and serve over rice.
tomatocurry.tip: Toast the dry spices in the pan for 20 seconds before adding liquids.

stickypork.title: Sticky sesame pork udon
steps: Sear pork in a hot skillet until cooked.
Add vegetables and cook until heated through.
Stir in noodles and sauces; toss until glossy, finish with sesame seeds.
stickypork.tip: Keep the pan hot so the vegetables don’t go soggy.

restaurant.title: Your regular restaurant breakfast
ingredients: A generous serving of breakfast potatoes
steps: Enjoy your usual Saturday and Sunday breakfast.
For planning, estimate approximately 850–1,100 kcal; restaurant recipes and portion sizes vary.
restaurant.tip: This is intentionally unchanged. No need to remove the rye bread from this meal.

shakechoc.title: Chocolate–banana shake (make 3)
steps: Blend oats with water first for a smoother drink.
Add the remaining ingredients and blend thoroughly.
Repeat for three shakes spread throughout Wednesday.
shakechoc.tip: Three shakes provide roughly 1,250–1,450 kcal and 125–150 g protein in total, depending on the whey. Use the label for precision.

shakeberry.title: Vanilla–berry shake (make 3)
steps: Blend oats with water first.
Add whey, nut butter, berries and ice; blend until creamy.
Repeat for three shakes spread throughout Wednesday.
shakeberry.tip: Whey smoothies alone are not a nutritionally complete long-term meal-replacement regimen.

notes: Nutrition figures are planning estimates, not measured values. Use ingredient labels and adjust portions to match targets.
On regular days add a protein-rich snack and optional 150–200 kcal dessert. Add a second shake or larger protein portion if needed.
Restaurant breakfast has substantial uncertainty; no fixed meal calories are promised.
Wednesday shakes are not nutritionally complete. Supplements do not make a low-variety liquid diet equivalent to balanced meals.
Cook chicken to 74°C/165°F; refrigerate leftovers promptly.
Morning supplements contribute some calories, especially collagen and fibre powder; check product labels.

Per-meal calories and protein, carbohydrate, and fat are rough estimates from common food composition values and typical package labels; brand, raw/cooked weight, sauce and oil can change the result substantially.
